parsed.explanation: The combined regime is hostile and traveller-facing: national passport/entry rules require sex assigned at birth, treat document or presentation discrepancies as possible misrepresentation, and can produce refusal, lifetime ineligibility, or detention where immigration-custody abuse is documented. The state adds a bathroom law enforced by ID checks in public buildings, a binary definition act barring marker changes, no gender-identity hate-crime or statewide anti-discrimination coverage, and a top 'Do Not Travel' tier for adult trans travellers. Minors face care bans and school erasure. Courts have enjoined some national orders and a passport suit is pending, but no remedy works at the border or in facilities. No execution or general criminalisation of trans identity is documented, keeping this above the 0.15 tier, but universal facility/document exposure and severe custody risk place it in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth, stop new X markers, and flag discrepancies; officers may refuse and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility. Existing X passports remain valid but are challenged.
entry_documents.protection: Passport litigation pending; legal-aid FAQ; some court injunctions. No documented border remedy for trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport marker plus presentation can trigger secondary screening, refusal, or referral to immigration detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, and sexual abuse of trans men; national prisons adopt conversion-style policies and deny care; state prison denied surgery.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national orders enjoined; state bathroom law does not govern cell assignment; no documented visitor custody remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border discrepancy can move into immigration detention with birth-sex custody and abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law requires restrooms match birth certificate in public schools, universities, prisons, and state buildings; fines are $25k/$125k; troopers checked IDs at capitol women's restrooms. National bans cover many states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trans women with female ID were admitted in one check; limited exemptions; no individual criminal penalty documented in this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor using a government facility may be ID-checked; facility fines pressure exclusion; state law does not reach all private venues.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors; national orders hostile to minor care and to prison care; adult visitor care is not documented.
care_services.protection: Injunctions blocked some national directives; five district attorneys refused; no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor needing care faces denial or child-abuse scrutiny; adult routine care is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; state parental-rights law mandates deadnaming and misgendering in schools.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says it will not target mere disagreement; courts enjoined some orders; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity but state statute does not.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing chills visibility and advocacy and raises surveillance/reporting risk.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans minor gender-affirming care and uses child-abuse investigation machinery; schools must deadname and misgender; bathroom law covers schools. National order threatens teachers.
minors_guardians.protection: Injunctions and district-attorney refusals limit some enforcement; no documented visitor-family exemption.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans minor in a public facility or care setting is exposed; parent or guardian may face scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity; police enforcement of bathroom ID checks can out visitors; violence figures are not baseline-comparable. LGB visibility is rolling back.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some city ordinances; no documented state-level gender-identity recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police called to a facility or street incident may check documents, increasing outing; bias prosecution is unlikely under state law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No effective border remedy; bathroom guidance unclear; top 'Do Not Travel' tier; school investigation outcome unknown; later enforcement is not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties passport suit, legal-aid FAQ, court injunctions; some city protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and post-hoc; they do not prevent border refusal, facility exclusion, or custody harm.

anchor_checks.comparison: Meridia's police extortion and overnight cells are more routine street-level predation than this jurisdiction's documented border/facility regime, but this jurisdiction adds possible lifetime entry bans and severe immigration-custody abuse; I place it similar to slightly below 0.25-B.

Vellandra's visitor register bars entry with exclusion and humiliation, but no imprisonment. This jurisdiction also refuses entry and can impose lifetime bans, and adds facility ID checks plus documented custody abuse, so it is lower than 0.35-A.

Kestrel Isles treats border discrepancies as secondary screening and administrative refusal. Here the same discrepancy can escalate to lifetime ineligibility and detention with documented abuse, so it is materially below 0.55-B.
The 0.75-C anchor has working remedies and no credible custody threat. This jurisdiction has pending, non-operative remedies, facility exclusion, and severe custody risk, so it is far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: National border rules and the state's bathroom law compound each other: a passport/presentation mismatch can trigger refusal, lifetime ineligibility, or detention, while using a state facility can trigger ID checks and exclusion. Immigration and prison custody carry documented abuse and denial of care. Minors face care bans and school erasure. Remedies exist on paper but are slow or unavailable at the border and in facilities. The jurisdiction is in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier for adult trans travellers, but no execution or general criminalisation of trans identity is documented, placing it above the 0.15 tier.
